# 01 Red Pill — voicing round (Batch 3A, the fat and driven set)

*Generated by tests/voicing/batch03a.py. Level reading: RMS over the note-on region of the spit riff (phrase i); matched to the bank reference (−18.0 dBFS RMS) by VOLUME; phrase (b)'s reading is in the table too. Every change is before → after under the echo rule. WAVs are on the listen/batch-03a-chapter1-fat-and-driven branch only.*

**Recommended: B centre** — a MONO bass of two saws at the same pitch 7.8 cents apart (beating 0.25 Hz at A1, 0.5 Hz at A2), tight: VINTAGE 10 (the card's wander s.d. 0.3 cents on a held A2, static offset -1.0), no LFO, no glide. A 24 dB low-pass (CUTOFF 92, KEY TRK 100, RESO 58) with a filter envelope that falls in 29 ms: the spit (the first 23 ms of the isolated A1 are 869 Hz against 414 Hz in the next 67 ms), and the per-voice DRIVE at 88 for the grit and the warmth (crest factor 4.8 dB against 8.9 at DRIVE 0; the centroid hardly moves, 622 against 650 Hz, because the drive sits before the filter). Centroid 622 Hz on the spit riff, 1406 Hz on the stabs; 51 % of the riff's energy sits under 60 Hz (the A1 fundamental, 55 Hz). The wet is a slap at 80 ms (ALLEY 62, FEEDBK 10, MIX 30) and a short spring (DRAIN 30, SIZE 40): its return is, at the loudest of the three isolated notes, -39.6 / -20.5 / -11.7 dB re the dry note in the 0-20 / 20-100 / 100-250 ms windows (every window under the note; the 100-250 ms window, where the 150 ms note is already dying, is the tightest); the voice alone is 60 dB down 30 ms after the key-up, with the wet 486 ms. Level -17.9 dBFS on the spit riff, -18.0 on phrase (b), peak -10.8, worst case 1047 host instr/sample. C is the grit axis: DRIVE 110 plus GROWL 46 (crest 4.6 dB, and +593 instr/sample), with the wet turned down (worst window -16.5 dB); D is the wet axis (worst windows -34.8 / -15.5 / -6.3 dB: the echo is nearly as loud as the note in the last window, which is too much).

## What to listen to

`*_spit.wav` is the one to judge (a sixteenth-note spit riff, then three isolated notes with silence after each: the wet return sits in those gaps), `*_riff.wav` is the pilot's low riff and `*_stabs.wav` the chord phrase.
Listen for: is B tight and stable under a vocal (no wobble), the grit (B against C's RAT-style GROWL), the warmth, and whether the slap and spring in B lift the presence without ever sounding like an effect. D is there to show where 'slight' ends.

*Notes.* Level is read on the note-on region of the spit riff (phrase i); phrase (b) is in the table with the difference. The wet is read per time window on the three isolated notes of phrase (i): the effects' own return (the render minus the same render with the slap and spring off) re the dry note's
RMS in that window; the dry is read as it falls, so the 100-250 ms window of a 150 ms note compares the return with a note that has already ended. The per-voice DRIVE sits before the filter (voices -> DRIVE -> filter), so it adds density and warmth and the later low-pass takes the edge back: the grit that survives is in
the 150-400 Hz band; GROWL (after the filter) is the RAT-style edge, at +578 instr/sample whenever it is on (C). MONO does not re-fire the envelopes on legato: the spit is a detached-note sound. Variant A is rendered through the base program path.
